From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - AtlasApps / Redwood

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the time today - great conversation. Quick recap of what we heard, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we have everything aligned before the technical deep-dive.

Pain points (from your team):
- High unit costs and unpredictable spend with current OpenAI usage (embeddings + chat).
- Vendor lock concerns and rate-limit-related outages during peak testing.
- Need for embedding schema compatibility (we must avoid a full reindex).
- Compliance evidence requests from procurement (SOC 2, audit logs, data residency).

Current stack (what you described):
- OpenAI for embeddings (semantic search) + Anthropic Claude for assistant/chat flows.
- Vector store: self-hosted Faiss on AWS; metadata in Postgres.
- Traffic profile: bursty nightly reindex and steady read-heavy production queries (95th percentile query size ~512 tokens).

Success criteria (your priorities):
- Latency: end-to-end inference p99 < 200ms for chat flows in US region.
- Compatibility: embeddings API drop-in or simple adapter to avoid reindexing.
- Cost: >=30% reduction in per-embedding unit cost without trading away quality.
- Security: ability to provide SOC2 evidence, VPC/private deployment options, and KMS-managed keys.

What Redwood can help with (summary):
- We can provide a migration path that includes an embeddings API adapter to preserve your existing vector schema, a shortlist of open models for both chat and embeddings, and a performance/cost estimate per workload.
- For compliance we will share SOC2 reports and provide an architecture pattern for Private deployment (VPC + KMS).

Attachments included with this message: Atlas_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (you sent earlier) and our preliminary Redwood_Model_Shortlist.xlsx (attached).

Next steps (agreed):
1) Technical deep-dive with your engineering + our inference team (1 hour) - propose Tue Jun 8, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT.
2) Share model shortlist + perf/cost estimates prior to the meeting.
3) Procurement/security will exchange the security questionnaire and initial SOC2 evidence.

If that looks right, I'll schedule the deep-dive and loop in our security lead (Neha).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Sam - thanks for the quick reply and for the embeddings schema. A few notes to address your asks and set expectations before the deep-dive: 

Model shortlist (high level):
- Llama 2 (70B) quantized variant - strong embedding + chat fidelity on longer contexts; expected higher memory but good quality.
- Mistral Instruct (7B) - cost-efficient chat model for many assistant flows; low latency and smaller footprint.
- RedPajama-INCITE (13B) fine-tuned for instruction-following - good middle ground for chat quality/cost.
- Open-embedding tuned variant (e.g., OpenCLIP-based or openly tuned 3-4B embedding models) for embedding replacement (we'll provide a connector).

Compatibility notes: 
- We will build an embeddings adapter layer that exposes an OpenAI-compatible embeddings API endpoint. That adapter will: accept the same input shape, return the same vector dimensionality and metadata fields, and apply a lightweight normalization step to match your existing vectors. Migration can be staged (dual-writing for verification, then switch reads). This approach avoids a full reindex in most cases.

Estimated perf & cost (preliminary):
- Expected embedding unit cost reduction: ~30-40% depending on model and instance types.
- Latency p95/p99 for chat: varies by model - Mistral 7B expected p99 ~120-180ms on our dedicated pool; Llama 70B quantized p99 ~180-300ms depending on sequence length; we'll finalize numbers with perf runs.

Pre-meeting deliverables (we'll share before Jun 8):
- Detailed perf/cost sheet per model (attached as perf_estimates.pdf).
- Architecture diagram for embeddings adapter and a migration plan (can demo dual-write approach).
- SOC2 evidence + security checklist answers (we'll include the requested items from Atlas_Security_Questionnaire.pdf).

Proposed attendees for the deep-dive: your platform engineers + procurement/legal, our inference lead, and our security lead (Neha). I'll send the invite for Tue Jun 8, 10:00 AM PT and include a short agenda: 1) perf baseline & model choices, 2) embeddings compatibility strategy, 3) security/procurement checklist.

Best,
Rishi
